newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates edge higher on firmer sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates edge higher on firmer sentiment.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates were steady to firmer on Tuesday with moderate activity seen in most regions although trade for ULCC and VLCC tonnage in the Mideast Gulf was slower today after a flurry of Demand on Monday, traders said.
However, rates for VLCCS in the region were mostly firmer reflecting Mondays busier chartering activity and sentiment for firmer prices as demand for December stems starts to pick up.

Mideast Gulf to the West valued around W57.5 while trips to Japan valued around W65 up five points but based of trade to S.Korea for 260,000 tonne at the same levels. Singapore voyages were five points at around W60.

The West African transatlantic trade remained thin although million barrel tonnage was booked at a slight higher W91.5 to the U.S. Atlantic Coast. Trade to the Europe saw Cepsa booking a million barrels into Spain but no rate was reported.
North Sea transatlantic activity remained dull but rates for inter-UKC trips were around 12.5 points firmer with W112.5 paid for Aframax tonnage while a Suezmax into a French refiner took W95.
In the Mediterranean, business was fairly brisk but rates were little better than steady as good avails of older tonnage capped gains for modern vessels.

Brokers said rates for cross-Med trips for Suezmax tonnage remained fairly strong at around W97.5 while Aframax rates for modern tonnage held around W107.5 although older tonnage was booked around five points under this level.
